Present : Sri J.N.Subramanya, B.A., L.L.M.,
 Chief Judge, Prl. M.A.C.T.,
 Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru.

Petitioner: Annadurai P.,
 S/o. Petchi Mudaliyar,
 Aged about 52 years,
 Residing at Samanwaya Road,
 Ward No.13, KRS Agrahara,
 Kunigal Town, Tumakuru District.
(By Sri G.P. Shivaprasad, Advocate)

-Vs- Respondents: 1. Srinivasa B.,
 S/o Late Baktavatsala,
 R/at Opp. to Urdu School,
 Upparahalli Road, Tumakuru.
 (Absent)
 2. Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd.,
 No.48, 3rd floor, SS corner building,
 Hospital Road, (next to Kamath Hotel),
 Shivaji Nagar, Benglauru,
 Karnataka - 560001.
 Policy No.418005/31/21/015098  valid from 25.03.2021 to 24.03.2022  (By Sri Kiran Pujar, Advocate)
 SCCH-1 2 MVC No.4415/2022  JUDGMENT Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-05-AE-7347 asserting

that on 05.08.2021 at about 6.30 p.m. when petitioner riding a motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-EY-1603 from Yediyuru towards Kunigal, on Bengaluru-Mangaluru road, near Syndicate Bank Building, KRS Agrahara, Kunigal Town,
Tumakuru District, driver of Car bearing No.KA-05- AE-7347, drove the same negligently, dashed Annadurai .P vs Srinivasa .B on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18826841/
1
the same to the hind part of the motorcycle, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.

2. Regarding accident Kunigal police registered crime No.228/2021 against the driver of the Car bearing No.KA- 05-AE-7347.
3.

Petitioner took treatment at Community Health Centre, Kunigal, Adichunchanagiri hospital,
Belluru, as on the date of accident petitioner being aged about 52 years, used to earn Rs.20,000/p.m. by working as Labour.
4. In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1-owner of the car remained absent.

5. In response to the notice, respondents No.2 appeared through his Advocate, filed written statement, denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of accident, age, occupation, income,
nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

The respondent No.2- insurance company submitted readiness to indemnify the respondent No.1 if as on the date of accident car had valid permit, FC etc.
6.

On the basis of the pleadings on 11.08.2023 , this Authority has framed the following issues :
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that on 05.08.2021 at about 6.30 p.m. near Syndicate Bank Building, B.M. Road, KRS Agrahara, Kunigal Town, Tumkuru, he met with an accident and sustained injuries, was due to actionable negligence act on the part of the driver of the Car bearing registration No.KA-05- AE-7347 as alleged?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled to compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order ?
7. On 10.10.2023, 16.02.2024 petitioner deposed as PW1 and produced 10 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.10

. 
8. I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of respondent No.2 and perused the records.

9. On the basis of the record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the affirmative Issue No.2 ...

Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.1,47,752/-
with current and future interest at 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
Annadurai .P vs Srinivasa .B on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18826841/
2 REASONS 10. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence petitioner stated that on 05.08.2021 at about 6.30 p.m. when riding a motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-EY-1603 from Yediyuru towards Kunigal, on Bengaluru-Mangaluru road, near Syndicate Bank Building, KRS Agrahara, Kunigal Town,
Tumakuru, driver of Car bearing No.KA-05-AE-7347, drove the same negligently, dashed the same to the hind part of the motorcycle, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
11.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the written statement respondent No.2 insurance company denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.

12. In the cross-examination petitioner stated that on the date of accident himself and his wife are traveling by sitting on the two-wheeler towards Kunigal town on the left side of the road, after the accident he was shifted to Government Hospital, Kunigal.
PW.1 stated that his daughter has filed complaint who did not witness the accident.
The petitioner has denied the suggestion that as the accident taken place due to his negligence, complaint was lodged after 14 days of the accident.

13. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR with complaint pertaining to crime No.228/2021 registered by Kunigal police against driver of Car bearing No.KA-05-AE-7347 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,337 of IPC regarding collision taken place on 05.08.2021 at 18.30 hours between motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-EY-1603 and Car bearing No.KA-05-AE-7347 resulting in the injuries to the petitioner, on the basis of the complaint presented by Pratheeksha daughter of the petitioner.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of the spot mahazar recorded on 20.08.2021.
Ex.P.3 is sketch of place of accident.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of vehicle seizure mahazars.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of motor vehicle accident report dated 24.09.2021.
Ex.P.6 is the copy of wound certificate in which reason for the injuries are noted as alleged RTA on 05.08.2021 at 6.40 p.m.

Ex.P.7 is the copy of the chargesheet filed by Kunigal police in crime No.228/2021 against respondent No.1- Srinivasa B. S/o Late Bakthavatsala - the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-05-AE-7347 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,337,338 of IPC, Sec.134(B), 187 of MV Act.
In the police records name of the petitioner is noted as rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-EY-1603 and injured of the accident.

14. In this case there are no reasons to disbelieve the contents of police records regarding reason,
mode and consequence of accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 05.08.2021 at about 6.30 p.m.
when petitioner riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-EY-1603 from Yediyuru towards Kunigal, on Bengaluru-Mangaluru road, near Syndicate Bank Building, KRS Agrahara, Kunigal Town,
Tumakuru, respondent No.1-Srinivasa B. negligently drove the Car bearing No.KA-05-AE-7347,
dashed the same to the hind part of the motorcycle, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:

In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident he has suffered cut lacerated wound over right forehead, abrasion over the right supro orbital morgun, abrasion on dorsum of right foot, abrasion right outer aspect of elbow and local tenderness for the right shoulder right clavical and greater tubertomy of humerous right, took treatment at CHC, Kunigal and Annadurai .P vs Srinivasa .B on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18826841/
3

Adichunchanagiri hospital, by spending Rs.50,000/- and required to take further treatment at the cost of Rs.50,000/-, as on the date of accident being aged about 52 years used to earn Rs.20,000/-p.m. by working as Labour.
16. In the written statement, respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
17. In the cross-examination, petitioner denied the suggestion that in the accident he has suffered simple injuries and never spent Rs.50,000/- for treatment.
PW.1 stated that prior to the accident he was working as Stores Incharge in Semi Labs Limited and earning Rs.50,000/- per month and after the accident he was removed from the job by the factory.
PW.1 submitted that non-production of documents regarding occupation and income.

18. The wound certificate, prescriptions, medical bills shows that in the accident petitioner suffered cut lacerated wound over right forehead, abrasion over the right supro orbital morgue, abrasion on dorsum of right foot, abrasion right outer aspect of elbow and local tenderness for the right shoulder, fracture of right clavicle and fracture of greater tuberomy of humerous right, took treatment at CHC Kunigal and Adichunchanagiri Hospital, Belluru at the cost of Rs.7,752/-.

entities.text: CHC Kunigal and Adichunchanagiri Hospital, Belluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 19. In the copy of Aadhar card the date of birth of the petitioner is noted as 18.05.1970.
In the file there are no documents regarding occupation and income of the petitioner.

Hence, I award Rs.45,000/- towards pain and sufferings, Rs.7,752/- towards treatment, Rs.5,000/- towards attendant, conveyance, nourishment charges, Rs.60,000/- (Rs.15,000 x4) towards loss of income during treatment period, Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities and future unhappiness.
20.
Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for Rs.1,47,752/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
21. In the written statement , respondent No.2 insurance company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to the Car bearing No.KA-05-AE-7347 as on the date of accident.
The copy of the permit shows that since 01.09.2021 to 31.08.2026 Car bearing No.KA-05-AE- 7347 had permit No.KA2021-CC-8003C to run in Karnataka.
In the file there are no documents to show that as on 05.08.2021 Car bearing No.KA-05-AE-7347 which is a Cab had permit to run in Karnataka.
Hence it is clear that as on the date of accident the respondent No.1 violated permit clause of the policy.

In view of the recent opinion of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka whenever insured violated the permit and fitness certificate clause of the policy, insurer is bound to deposit the compensation amount reserving the liberty to recover so deposited amount from the insured.
Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondent No.1 is not entitle to be indemnified by the respondent No.2/insurance company.

However, the respondent No.2 insurer is liable to deposit the compensation amount reserving liberty to recover the same from the respondent No.1 by taking steps before jurisdictional MACT in accordance with law.

Hence, I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative and pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.

Annadurai .P vs Srinivasa .B on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18826841/
4
The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.1,47,752/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.

The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-05-AE-7347 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today,
reserving liberty to recover the same from respondent No.1 who violated the permit clause of the policy by taking steps before jurisdictional MACT in accordance with law.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.

It is clarified that respondent No.1 may insist respondent No.2-insurance company to indemnify by producing document to show that as on 05.08.2021 Car bearing No.
KA-05-AE-7347 had permit to run in Karnataka.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.

(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
